# Parameter estimation {#sec-parameter-estimation}

In the [previous chapter](hybrid-models.qmd), we composed a graphical model from regression kernels whose parameters were given as fixed numbers. But where did those numbers come from? In this chapter, we treat parameter estimation as a special case of the conditioning machinery we have already developed: parameters are unknown quantities, and data inform our beliefs about them through Bayes' rule.

We begin by showing how the graphical model from @sec-swiss-health-model can be augmented with parameter nodes to represent uncertainty about the regression coefficients and noise scales. Conditional independence then justifies fitting each regression kernel separately — a key simplification. After working through the full Bayesian treatment, we introduce maximum likelihood and maximum a posteriori estimation as convenient shortcuts and connect them back to the graphical framework.
